newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's KDD to halt 'call-back' service.
newsitem.headline: Japan's KDD to halt 'call-back' service.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd and two other Japanese international carriers said on Thursday they would halt "call-back" discount services when they are seen degrading the firms' proprietary networks.

KDD, International Digital Corp and International Telecom Japan Inc, suffering from the erosion of their customer base due to the spread of call-back services, said they would take the step immediately after the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry allows revision of their business rules.

The move follows a resolution by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a United Nations agency, last October that two kinds of call-back services -- answer suppression and polling -- should be prohibited because they degrade other operators' networks.
In a call-back service, users call a switching centre, usually in the United States, and make discount international phone calls using American operators' low-cost lines.
Most call-back service providers use Japanese operators' networks free of charge to ring American switching centres.
American telephone giant AT&T Corp recently launched a call-back service in Japan, but it uses its own lines to call the U.S. switching centre.
